question: Should OpenClaw retain grouped Claw update planning as an experiment-gated core lifecycle primitive, with this read-only planner as the consent boundary for the remaining stacked work?
rationale: The patch creates a new persisted-state, CLI, capability-escalation, and consent contract that cannot be safely accepted or redirected by automated review alone.

options.title: Sponsor the bounded core primitive
options.body: Keep the planner in core behind `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`, subject to exact-head proof and review of the prerequisite/follow-on stack.

options.title: Narrow the contract
options.body: Retain only diagnostics or planning surfaces that have a clear core owner, and move unsupported grouped-update behavior out of this stack.

options.title: Pause the stack
options.body: Defer the experimental Claw lifecycle until maintainers settle its long-term core versus extension ownership.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the bounded core primitive
recommendation.body: Keep the planner in core behind `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`, subject to exact-head proof and review of the prerequisite/follow-on stack.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is assigned and provided the most concrete review direction on the planner’s lifecycle and ownership invariants.
